Conversation, family & daily routines · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

inside preposition and adverb

also within (a place), indoors, is your father in?, is he in?, in (at home), in (motion), go in

classical

Cic. Att. 3.10.2: intrā parietēs meōs
Plaut. Mil. 596: Cohibēte intrā līmen etiam vōs parumper

intrā

preposition with the accusative

inside, within

Within a boundary, at rest or going in: intrā parietēs, within one’s walls; intrā portam penetrāre pedem, to set foot inside the gate. Classically only a preposition (Lewis & Short); the adverb is intus. For “within” a time, see within (a time).

Other words

  • intus — inside, indoors

    adverb · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 569: estne frāter intus?; Cic. Cat. 2.11: intus est hostis; Traupman 101: estne pater intus?; Traupman 332

    Where a thing is: inside, at home. For going in, intrō (see into).

  • intrō — in, inside (with motion)

    adverb of motion · also used · classical · Traupman 332

    Intrō answers “where to?”, intus “where?”: intrō īre, to go in; intus esse, to be in.

Examples

  • Cohibēte intrā līmen etiam vōs parumper, Pleusiclēs

    You stay inside the door a little longer too, PleusiclesPlaut. Mil. 596

  • neque hūc umquam, postquam nātus sum, intrā portam penetrāvī pedem

    and never since I was born have I set foot inside the gate herePlaut. Men. 399–400

  • quod facile fuisset nisi intrā parietēs meōs dē meā perniciē cōnsilia inīrentur

    which would have been easy, had plots for my ruin not been laid within my own wallsCic. Att. 3.10.2

  • sed estne frāter intus? — Nōn est.

    But is my brother indoors? — He isn’t.Ter. Ad. 569

  • fīcī enim sēmen nātūrāle intus in eā fīcō, quam edimus, quae sunt minūta grāna

    for the fig’s natural seed is inside the fig we eat: those are the tiny grainsVarr. RR 1.41.4

See also outside, into, within, build.
